purpose: Living registry of the evidence behind every factor in impact-factors.json. We track these sources for updates and revise factors as better data appears. Each factor lists the sources consulted, the figure taken, and any better source we are still chasing.
reviewCadence: monthly, plus whenever a provider or major study publishes new figures

sources.title: Energy use of AI inference, efficiency pathways, and test-time scaling
TokenPowerBench: Benchmarking the Power Consumption of LLM Inference (AAAI 2026)
Quantifying Energy & Carbon of LLM Inference via Simulations

whPer1kOutputTokens.chasing: A directly measured per-token figure for Claude models specifically.

inputTokenEnergyRatio.unit: fraction of an output token's energy

sources.title: Prefill vs. Decode Bottlenecks: SRAM-Frequency Tradeoffs and the Memory-Bandwidth Ceiling
sources.figure: prefill <=3.4% of energy vs decode >=96% for standard generation

inputTokenEnergyRatio.chasing: Per-token prefill energy as a function of context length (quadratic attention) for long agentic contexts.

cacheReadEnergyRatio.unit: fraction of an output token's energy per cached input token
cacheReadEnergyRatio.priority: Dominant term for agentic workloads. Now corroborated by two independent lines; still worth a direct energy measurement.
cacheReadEnergyRatio.grounding: Two lines converge on ~0.005: (a) Anthropic cache-read price = 0.1x input; (b) measured 85-95% cost/energy saving on a cache hit => cache read = 5-15% of fresh input = 0.0025-0.0075x output. Per-cached-token structure matches how the saving is measured and priced.

sources.title: Anthropic prompt caching pricing (cache read ~0.1x input price)
Prompt Caching in 2026: Cut LLM Costs, Keep Quality
sources.figure: 85-95% cost/energy saving on cache hit; collapses prefill compute into a memory read

sources.title: Don't Break the Cache: Prompt Caching for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

cacheReadEnergyRatio.chasing: A directly measured KV-cache read energy (cache-hit vs miss joules) over long-context decode, e.g. via ML.ENERGY-style GPU power measurement, to confirm the 0.005 mid-point.

sources.title: TokenPowerBench per-token range 0.0001-0.002 Wh by model size

modelTiers.chasing: Measured per-model energy from the ML.ENERGY leaderboard (https://ml.energy/leaderboard) and Hugging Face AI Energy Score (https://huggingface.co/spaces/AIEnergyScore). Anthropic does not publish active parameter counts.

sources.title: The carbon and water footprints of data centers
sources.figure: US regional ~321 gCO2e/kWh; global ~396; US hosts ~45% of AI datacentre capacity

gridGCo2PerKwh.chasing: Datacentre-region-aware and time-of-day intensity (e.g. Electricity Maps), reflecting where Claude actually runs.

sources.title: AI water usage per query, real 2026 numbers
Data centre water consumption (npj Clean Water)

waterOnsiteMlPerWh.chasing: Anthropic/hosting-provider region-level WUE disclosures; adjustment for liquid-cooled AI racks.

waterOffsiteMlPerWh.unit: mL per Wh (offsite, electricity-generation consumptive water)

sources.title: EIA: US electric power sector water efficiency
sources.figure: US thermoelectric consumptive ~1.25 L/kWh; nuclear ~2.1, coal ~2, CCGT ~1.2 or less

sources.title: AI Data Centers and the Water Use Feedback Loop
sources.figure: offsite comparable to or larger than onsite; total 5-20x onsite alone

waterOffsiteMlPerWh.chasing: US-grid-mix consumptive intensity tracked yearly (coal decline lowers it); reconcile the LBNL 7.6 L/kWh upper estimate vs EIA consumptive.
